blocks.text: Naturally occurring particulate matter includes dust from the earth's surface and biological material such as pollen, spores and animal debris. Volcanic eruptions can put very large quantities of gases and particulate matter into the atmosphere, and lightning produces significant quantities of oxides of nitrogen. Other natural sources are algae on the ocean surface, which give out hydrogen sulfide; wind erosion, which introduces particulate matter; and humid zones such as swamps, peat bogs and shallow lakes, which produce methane.

blocks.prompt: Identify and briefly explain three major natural sources of air pollutants (exercise Q.2a).
blocks.explanation: Volcanoes eject enormous amounts of sulfur gases, ash and dust; lightning heats air so that nitrogen and oxygen combine to nitrogen oxides; and wetlands such as swamps release methane from the anaerobic decay of plant matter. Dust storms, pollen and ocean algae giving hydrogen sulfide are further examples.

items: Natural: dust, pollen and spores (PM); volcanoes (gases, PM); lightning (NOx); ocean algae (H2S); wind erosion (PM); swamps and bogs (CH4).
